newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-LAUDRUP ANGERS HIBS FANS AS RANGERS WIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LAUDRUP ANGERS HIBS FANS AS RANGERS WIN.

text.p: Rangers came from behind to beat Hibernian 2-1 and maintain their 14-point lead at the top of the Scottish premier divison on Saturday as Celtic won 5-0 at home to Motherwell.
But Rangers Danish skipper Brian Laudrup was branded a "cheat" by Hibs fans at Easter Road as Walter Smith's flu-hit side battled for a vital victory.
Laudrup was involved in a controversial penalty incident which enabled German Jorg Albertz to score the winner 18 minutes from time.
Hibs goalkeeper Jim Leighton challenged Laudrup, who tumbled to the ground after he outstripped the Hibs defence.

The referee pointed to the spot, Leighton was booked for dissent and after Albertz scored the Hibs fans chanted "cheat, cheat" at Laudrup who they felt gained an unfair advantage from stage-managing his fall.
Rangers had to come from behind, with their Danish striker Erik Bo Andersen cancelling out a seventh minute goal from Kevin Harper after 11 minutes.
It was Rangers fifth successive victory and kept them 14 points ahead of arch-rivals Celtic, who have two games in hand.
The Scottish League had turned down a late request from Rangers to have the match postponed because of a flu virus at the club.
Celtic were the highest scorers of the day although none of the goals in their 5-0 rout of Motherwell was scored by a Scot.
Portuguese striker Jorge Cadete scored twice, while Italian Paolo di Canio, Dutchman Pierre Van Hooydonk and Dane Morten Wieghorst scored the others.
Third-placed Dundee United beat Kilmarnock 2-0 while fourth-placed Hearts came back from conceding a first-minute goal to bottom club Raith to win 2-1.
